articles.title: Stock markets fall after US CPI disappointment, no to Swedish Social Democratic government today
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Yesterday's unexpectedly high US CPI weighs on risk appetite, 
driven by falling prices for IT hardware, given the risk that higher interest rates could slow down the rollout of AI infrastructure. The declines in the US (where both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell just over 1 percent) have continued in Asia, with sharp stock market falls in Japan (-5%), China (-2%) and not least Korea (-8%). Futures point to continued declines in both the US and Europe today. U.S. bond yields initially rose but then fell back as investors rotated out of the stock market, while the dollar has weakened. Market expectations of the Fed have fluctuated overnight; from pricing in a nearly 50% probability of an October hike immediately after the data, expectations have tipped back towards most likely unchanged (7 basis points) and a total of just under three hikes until the end of next year. Strong stock markets have been highlighted by the Fed as supportive of the economy even as long-term interest rates have risen. Yesterday's Fed speakers Goolsbee and Daly (non-voters) both expressed concern about the CPI data but with different conclusions. Goolsbee warned of overheating from the AI rollout while Daly saw the need for further rate hikes, but without urgency. 
The Fed's 
Beige Book
showed signs of some slowdown in economic activity and in the labour market, but increased price pressures, although without any dramatic changes in the descriptions of the economy. Oil prices have fallen in a continued uncertain situation in the war with Iran (read the latest update from Erik Meyersson 
here
). Ukraine accuses the US of restricting access to intelligence via Starlink and Zelenskyy tells the Financial Times that Ukraine will resume attacks on Russian refineries, contrary to Trump's request. 
The monthly change in the CPI
 (US) was a tenth above ours and the consensus forecast and price increases were also broadly based. Several Fed members have indicated that the Fed should take a break in October and we are so far sticking to our belief in unchanged interest rates, but the pressure for a December hike has increased. Read more in our comment 
here
. 
Today's US data may contribute to the picture for the Fed. 
The PPI provides input to the forecast for the Fed's target variable core PCE for September (released on 29/10, after the interest rate announcement). Our preliminary estimate after the CPI is 0.31% m/m, which would be the fastest pace since May. Retail sales were surprisingly strong in August, albeit after two weak summer months. Continued unexpected strength in September would add to concerns in the Fed that it will be easier for companies to pass on cost increases to consumers. The manufacturing indices for New York and Philadelphia can show whether the faster pace in manufacturing will continue; however, these indices are volatile. Developments in the Middle East and for energy prices will also be important ahead of the October announcement, and on Friday morning you can listen to Fed Chairman Warsh talking with IMF Governor Georgieva at the IMF's annual meeting in Bangkok. Warsh has previously downplayed the signs of an improving inflation trend and has now gotten some support for his views.  
In Europe, we will keep our eyes on the EU summit on 15-16 October.
 Areas such as competitiveness, the EU's next long-term budget, security and defence, Ukraine and migration will be covered. It will be particularly interesting if trade relations with China are mentioned after last week's deliberations on, among other things, voluntary Chinese export restrictions on hybrid cars. 
Increased optimism among Swedish CFOs. 
According to the CFO Survey from Deloitte and SEB, Swedish CFOs are significantly more optimistic about business opportunities and financial prospects compared to last spring. You can read the full report 
here
 (in Swedish but with an English summary at the end).
Nordic key stories
Swedish unemployment, according to the Swedish Public Employment Service, 
continued to decline in September, from 6.5 to 6.4%. This data has shown a decline since the middle of last year, while the LFS trend (Statistics Sweden), for which we will get data tomorrow, is more difficult to interpret. 
Higher energy prices are expected to cause Swedish inflation expectations 
to rise for the shorter 1-year horizon, while the outlook 2 years ahead is uncertain, given a possible reversal of food VAT. 5-year expectations have been stable and close to the 2%-target.
The Swedish Riksdag will vote at 12:00 on whether Magdalena Andersson (Social Democratic Party) can form a government.
 Since the Left Party is sticking to its no to all governments in which the party is not a member, Andersson will be voted down. Most interesting will be how the Center Party, which had wished for a centrist government that also included the Christian Democrats, will vote. If the Riksdag cannot approve a new government after four votes, Sweden will proceed to an extraordinary election. This means that the pressure on the parties will increase with each vote, and probably especially for the opposition, which has begun to decline in public opinion in relation to the Tidö parties in the current government.
In Norway, we get Norges Bank's Lending Survey for Q3
, which does not tend to be a market mover.

articles.title: Börsfall efter KPI-besvikelse i USA, nej till S-regering idag
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Gårdagens oväntat höga USA-KPI tynger riskaptiten, 
drivet av fallande kurser på IT-hårdvara, givet risken för att högre räntor kan bromsa utbyggnaden av AI-infrastruktur. Nedgångarna i USA (där både S&P 500 och Nasdaq backade drygt 1 procent) har fortsatt i Asien, med kraftiga börsfall i Japan (-5%), Kina (-2%) och inte minst Korea (-8%). Terminerna pekar på fortsatta nedgångar i både USA och Europa i dag. Amerikanska obligationsräntor steg initialt men föll sedan tillbaka när investerare roterade ur börsen, medan dollarn har försvagats. Marknadens förväntningar på Fed har svängt under natten; från att ha prisat nästan 50% sannolikhet för en oktoberhöjning direkt efter statistiken har förväntningarna åter tippat tillbaka mot mest troligt oförändrat (7 punkter) och totalt knappt tre höjningar fram till slutet av nästa år. Starka börser har av Fed lyfts fram som stöttande för ekonomin även när långa räntor stigit. Gårdagens Fed-talare Goolsbee och Daly (inte röstande) uttryckte båda oro för KPI-statistiken men med olika slutsatser. Goolsbee varnade för överhettning från AI-utbyggnaden medan Daly såg behov av ytterligare räntehöjningar, men utan brådska. 
Feds 
Beige Book
visade tecken på viss dämpning av den ekonomiska aktiviteten och på arbetsmarknaden, men ökat pristryck, dock utan några dramatiska förändringar i beskrivningarna av ekonomin. Oljepriset har sjunkit i ett fortsatt osäkert läge i kriget med Iran (läs senaste uppdatering från Erik Meyersson 
här
). Ukraina anklagar USA för att ha begränsat tillgången till underrättelseinformation via Starlink och Zelenskyj säger till Financial Times att Ukraina kommer att återuppta attackerna på ryska raffinaderier, på tvärs mot Trumps begäran. 
Månadsförändringen i KPI
 (USA) var en tiondel över vår och konsensusprognosen och priserna steg dessutom på ganska bred front. Flera Fed-ledamöter har indikerat att Fed bör ta en paus i oktober och vi håller än så länge fast vid vår tro på oförändrad ränta, men trycket på en decemberhöjning har ökat. Läs mer i vår kommentar 
här
. 
Dagens USA-data kan bidra till bilden för Fed. 
PPI ger input till prognosen för Feds målvariabel kärn-PCE för september (släpps 29/10, efter räntebeskedet). Vårt preliminära estimat efter KPI är 0,31% m/m, vilket skulle vara den snabbaste takten sedan i maj. Detaljhandelsförsäljningen var överraskande stark i augusti, om än efter två svaga sommarmånader. Fortsatt oväntad styrka i september skulle spä på oron i Fed för att företagen får det lättare att skicka vidare kostnadsökningar till konsument. Industriindexen för New York och Philadelphia kan visa om det högre tempot i industrin håller i sig; dessa index är dock volatila. Utvecklingen i Mellanöstern och för energipriserna blir också viktig inför oktoberbeskedet och på fredag morgon kan man lyssna på Fed-ordförande Warsh som samtalar med IMF-chefen Georgieva vid IMF:s årsmöte i Bangkok. Warsh har tidigare tonat ned tecknen på en förbättrad inflationstrend och har nu fått ytterligare vatten på sin kvarn. 
I Europa kommer vi att hålla ögonen på EU-toppmötet 15-16 oktober.
 Områden som konkurrenskraft, EU:s nästa långtidsbudget, säkerhet och försvar, Ukraina och migration kommer att täckas in. Det blir särskilt intressant om handelsrelationerna med Kina nämns efter förra veckans överläggningar kring bl a frivilliga kinesiska exportbegränsningar för hybridbilar. 
Lästips: 
Starkare framtidstro hos svenska finanschefer. 
Enligt CFO Survey från Deloitte och SEB är svenska finanschefer betydligt mer optimistiska kring affärsmöjligheter och finansiella utsikter jämfört med i våras. Läs hela rapporten 
här
.
Sverige
Arbetsförmedlingens arbetslöshetsstatistik
 fortsatte att sjunka under september, från 6,5 till 6,4%. Statistiken har visat en nedgång sedan mitten av i fjol, medan AKU-statistiken (SCB), där vi får data i morgon, är mer svårtolkad. 
Högre energipriser väntas få inflationsförväntningarna 
att stiga för den kortare 1-årshorisonten, medan utsikterna på 2 års sikt är osäkra, givet bl a en möjlig reversering av matmomsen. 5-åriga förväntningar har varit stabila nära målet. 
Riksdagen röstar kl. 12:00 om Magdalena Andersson (S) får bilda regering.
 Eftersom Vänstern håller fast vid sitt nej till alla regeringar där partiet inte ingår kommer Andersson röstas ned. Mest spännande blir hur centern, som egentligen hade önskat sig en mittenregering där även KD ingår, ställer sig. Kan riksdagen inte godkänna en ny regering efter fyra omröstningar går Sverige vidare till ett extraval. Det innebär att pressen på partierna kommer att öka för varje omröstning och sannolikt särskilt för oppositionen som börjat backa i opinionen i förhållande till Tidö-partierna.

articles.title: Starkare framtidstro hos svenska finanschefer
articles.heading: Deloitte/SEB CFO Survey
articles.fulltext:
Svenska finanschefer är betydligt mer optimistiska kring affärsmöjligheter och finansiella utsikter jämfört med i våras. Fler tror på ökad tillväxt, förbättrade marginaler och högre aktivitet på transaktionsmarknaden. Det visar höstens CFO Survey från Deloitte och SEB.
Undersökningen genomfördes mellan 8 - 25 september
--- --- ---
English summary
 at the bottom
--- --- ---
Den makroekonomiska miljön under 2026 har varit minst sagt utmanande, men trots kraftigt stigande energipriser har världsekonomin visat tillväxtmässig motståndskraft. Med stigande faktisk inflation, och risker tydligt på uppsidan, har förväntningarna på centralbanker skiftat åt det hökaktiga hållet och räntehöjningar. De kraftigt stigande långa statsobligationsräntorna har dessutom förstärkt motvinden. Trots detta har flera indikatorer förbättrats under hösten, samtidigt som ekonomisk data har bekräftat en relativt god tillväxtutveckling i många länder.
Affärsmöjligheter och finansiella utsikter
Indikatorn för affärsmöjligheter stiger markant och når inte bara sin högsta nivå sedan våren 2022, utan ligger nu också i linje med det historiska genomsnittet sedan 2013. Utvecklingen drivs av en tydlig förändring i synen på marknadsläget: 
färre bedömer affärsmöjligheterna som genomsnittliga eller mindre fördelaktiga, 
samtidigt som andelen som ser dem som fördelaktiga har fördubblats jämfört med föregående mätning. Sammantaget pekar resultaten på en tydlig förskjutning mot en mer positiv syn på affärsmöjligheterna under de kommande sex månaderna.
Prioriteringar, strategiska möjligheter och riskbild
Höstens resultat visar en förskjutning från ett restriktivt tillväxtfokus till en mer balanserad agenda. Kostnadskontroll förblir högsta prioritet medan organisk tillväxt och operativa investeringar i kapacitet ökar i prioritering jämfört med i vårens undersökning. Samtidigt har riskbilden förändrats: pressade marginaler och priser anses vara den främsta utmaningen, medan oron för geopolitisk risk och svag ekonomisk tillväxt har minskat.
Att läget ser genomgående bättre ut i höstens undersökning går också igenom bedömningen av hur finansiella risker utvecklas. Den övergripande bilden är att vi ligger nära ett normalläge både i bedömningar men också historiska genomsnitt på olika frågeställningar. Tilltron kring motpartsrisk förbättras, medan synen på utlåningsviljan försämrats något. För den frågan är dock en historisk jämförelse svår eftersom synen på utlåningsviljan tydligt påverkas av lågräntemiljön som rådde de första åren då frågan ställdes.
Hot Topic: 
Höstens Hot Topic undersöker hur AI påverkar ekonomifunktionen, både utifrån hur organisationer styr och följer upp användningen och vilka processer och roller som redan håller på att förändras. Frågorna sträcker sig från prioritering till praktisk tillämpning och de hinder som finns.
Läs hela undersökningen genom view report ovan eller på undersökningens hemsida 
www.cfosurvey.se
För SEB’s pressmeddelande se 
https://sebgroup.com/sv/press/pressmeddelanden
Vilka av följande affärsstrategier kommer sannolikt vara en prioritet för ditt företagunder de närmaste 12 månaderna?
Källa:  Deloitte, SEB, Demoskop
Anta att ni idag har överskottslikviditet, hur skulle ni vilja använda era likvida medel under de kommande 6 månaderna?
Källa:  Deloitte, SEB, Demoskop
- - - -
English summary
The macroeconomic environment during 2026 has been challenging, to say the least, but despite sharply rising energy prices, the global economy has demonstrated resilience in terms of growth. With rising actual inflation and risks clearly tilted to the upside, expectations regarding central banks have shifted in a hawkish direction, pointing toward interest rate hikes. Furthermore, the sharp increase in long-term government bond yields has intensified these headwinds. Even so, several indicators have improved during the autumn, while economic data has confirmed relatively healthy growth trends in many countries.
Business conditions and financial prospects
The indicator for business opportunities is rising significantly, not only reaching its highest level since the spring of 2022, but now also aligning with the historical average since 2013. This development is driven by a clear shift in perspective on the market climate: fewer respondents view business opportunities as average or less favorable, while the proportion viewing them as favorable has doubled compared to the previous measurement. Overall, the results point to a clear shift toward a more positive outlook on business opportunities over the next six months.
Priorities, Strategic prospects, and Risk assessments
The autumn results show a transition from a restrictive growth focus to a more balanced agenda. Cost control remains the highest priority, while organic growth and operational investments in capacity have increased in priority compared to the spring survey. At the same time, the risk landscape has changed: squeezed margins and prices are considered the primary challenge, whereas concerns regarding geopolitical risk and weak economic growth have declined.
The generally more positive outlook in the autumn survey is also reflected in the assessment of how financial risks are evolving. The overall picture is that we are close to a normal state, both in terms of assessments and historical averages across various issues. Confidence regarding counterparty risk is improving, whereas the perception of lending appetite has deteriorated slightly. However, for this specific question, a historical comparison is difficult because the view of lending appetite is clearly influenced by the low-interest-rate environment that prevailed during the first few years the question was asked.
Hot Topic
The autumn Hot Topic survey examines how AI is impacting the finance function, looking at both how organizations govern and monitor its usage, and which processes and roles are already undergoing change. The questions range from prioritization to practical application and existing barriers.

articles.title: High CPI but probably not in itself enough to tip the scales for October
articles.heading: US Economy
articles.fulltext:
August CPI surprised on the upside for a 0.3% m/m increase, beating the consensus (0.2% m/m) for the second consecutive month. The surprise was broadly based and the annualized 3-month change for core CPI is now back above 3%. Several members have indicated that they want to see more data before hiking again, which has raised the bar for another increase already at the 28 October meeting. We think the totality of data this week will decide but stick to unchanged in October for now. 
Key points
Core CPI 0.3%, 2.6% y/y, consensus 0.2%, 2.5%, previous 0.3%, 2.4%
Headline CPI 0.6%, 3.7%, consensus 0.6%, 3.6% y/y, previous 0.4%, 3.4% y/y
The upside surprise was broadly based for both goods and services
Our preliminary estimate for core PCE is 0.31%
Several Fed members have said that the Fed can wait before hiking again
We think totality of data this week will decide the October decision
The outcome will support Warsh’s view that the inflation trend has not “meaningfully” improved
Broadly based increases
Core CPI increased by 0.33% in September, above our and the consensus expectations for a slightly above 0.2% month-on-month increase. The year-on-year rate increased from 2.4% to an above expectation of 2.6%. The surprise was broadly based. The monthly increases in goods prices (core goods 0.25%, core goods ex used cars and trucks 0.18%) and rents (0.33%) were all 0.1-0.15 percentage points above our forecast. Services excluding rents were also higher than expected. Tourist services, air tickets (1.2%) and hotels (2.0%), contributed to faster price increases though in both cases slowing from the previous month. Headline CPI (0.6% m/m) was in line with estimates. Energy prices increased slightly less than our forecast but at a solid pace (5% m/m) while food prices were unchanged. 
Second consecutive disappointment 
The monthly price changes for the core CPI are still within the volatile range during the past two years. Monthly core CPI has tended to surprise on the downside this year but has been higher than expected during August and September. The 3-month annualized change is now at the high end of the recent range and above 3%. This will concern some members of the Fed, who often focuses on this measure. 
Preliminary estimate for core PCE is 0.31%
The core PCE has remained the Fed’s key inflation objective. Our preliminary estimate for core PCE in September, given the information in the CPI, is 0.31%. Tomorrow’s September PPI will provide more input for the core PCE, however. 
Enough for an October rate hike?
Several Fed members have indicated that they want to evaluate the effects of the September rate hike before tightening again, most likely at the December meeting. This raises the bar for another increase at the 28 October meeting. Before the September CPI, markets priced a small 20% probability for an October hike. After the data, markets are back to pricing almost 50% probability for an increase. Data during the rest of the week (PPI, retail sales and industrial production) and anecdotal comments in the Fed’s Beige Book will also be important to watch for both the implications for PCE inflation and for growth and pricing power. August retail sales surprised strongly on the upside and another very strong report in September may signal increased scope for companies to pass through cost increases to customers. We stick to our view of an unchanged rate at the October meeting but the totality of data this week, as well as the events in the Middle East and energy prices, will be important. 
Also of interest will be the fireside chat with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the IMF’s managing direction Kristalina Georgieve early Friday morning. Kevin Warsh does not want to guide markets but his hawkish comments at both Jackson Hole and after the September meeting have tended to raise market expectations for rate hikes. Kevin Warsh has said that he is focusing on the broader trend rather than individual months, but had already earlier concluded that the slowdown in the CPI was not enough to convince him that the trend had meaningfully improved. The September data will not change his views on the trend. 
Short-term upside risks have increased
The renewed increase in energy prices has delayed the slowdown for headline inflation and has raised the risks for indirect effects from, for instance, higher transportation costs. Some signs of higher goods prices are emerging, and we have revised our near-term forecast slightly higher. There are also some signs that rents could start to rise at a slightly higher rate again, judging from the changes in market-based Zillow rents. This could reflect increased demand for rentals, driven by deteriorating affordability to purchase a home on the back of higher mortgage rates. Wage inflation continues to slow, however, which implies that any upturn in inflation will be temporary. The inflation outlook is significantly more uncertain than normal, but we continue to predict that underlying inflation trends will improve as temporary impulses from tariffs, energy prices and the AI build-out fade. Our forecast implies that both core CPI and core PCE will back at the target by the end of 2028.

articles.title: Consumption rose in September following large downward revision to August data
articles.heading: Swedish growth indicators
articles.fulltext:
Household consumption rose by 1.1% m/m in September
, contrary to our forecast of a small setback. However, substantial revisions to previous data 
lowered the level of consumption in August by 1.3pp
 compared with the previous estimate. We have flagged that, as the estimate for household consumption is now being published almost a month earlier than before, there is a risk that both volatility and revisions will increase significantly. This may be what we are seeing in today’s revisions. Unfortunately, such large potential revisions make the indicator a less reliable gauge of actual developments. Nonetheless, many factors point to strong growth in household consumption, and the year-on-year rate (3.5%) was broadly in line with our estimate (3.2%).
Growth was recorded in most subindices, with furniture and household equipment showing the fastest growth rate compared with last year. Clothing and shoes, as well as transportation and recreation, have also risen clearly year-on-year.
Sentiment indicators suggest that momentum in consumption is strong, and consumer confidence increased in September to its highest level since 2022, but the upturn in consumption is expected to face some headwinds over the next six months from rising energy prices and early rate hikes by the Riksbank. A turnaround in the labour market will be important in determining whether consumption will continue to grow at a high pace in 2027.

articles.title: Singapore’s MAS Hits Pause, Not Stop
articles.heading: Asia Alert
articles.fulltext:
Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) held policy steady, citing narrowing positive output gap through 2027. Yet, with inflation risks persisting, MAS left the door open to resume tightening next year. Already hugging the upper bound, the S$NEER has little room for near-term rally putting upside risks to our end-2026 USD/SGD forecast at 1.26. Still, with policy bias leaning hawkish, any pullback in the Singdollar will be brief. 
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) maintained policy settings, as we had expected. 
We estimate the rate of appreciation of the currency basket to have been maintained at 1.25% pa. There was no change to the width of the policy band and the level at which the band is centered. As a small and open economy, monetary policy in Singapore targets the exchange rate rather than interest rates. Specifically, MAS manages the Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (S$NEER) and ensures that the currency basket trades within the range of the policy band. While MAS has adjusted the center of the band a number of times in the last few years, the rate of appreciation of the slope is the most commonly adjusted tool. The width of the band is the least frequently changed, which we currently estimate to be around +/-2% around the center. 
Ahead of the meeting, the market had largely priced in continued tightening, though expectations softened slightly in the final stretch. 
In a Bloomberg survey, 17 out of 20 analysts expected an overall tighter stance, with the same ratio expecting another increase in the appreciation rate. No analyst expected a change in the center of the band, nor the width of the policy band. Typically, the S$NEER would already be hugging the top of the band ahead of actual tightening if the market felt strongly about the policy adjustment. The S$NEER was flirting with the upper bound of the policy band through most of September. Yet, we note the S$NEER marginally pulled back from the boundary in the last couple of weeks, suggesting some fading of market expectations (Chart 1). Indeed, 
we estimate the S$NEER to be trading around 1.71% above the center after the policy announcement. 
Chart 1: Market expectations of further tightening keeps S$NEER hugging the upper band
Source: Bloomberg, SEB
MAS expects the positive output gap to narrow through 2027. 
Advance estimates show Q3 GDP growth moderating to 5.4% y/y from an upwardly revised 6.2% in Q2. Although expansion remains well-above trend, policymakers anticipate AI-driven momentum will cool in the latter half of 2027.Even so, rising high-frequency indicators point to a re-acceleration through H1 2027. Aside from some weakness in the consumer-facing sector, growth across the rest of the segments remains robust. 
Overall, the growth outlook justifies today’s pause in policy tightening
.
Chart 2: Elevated imported inflation keeps upward pressure on MAS Core inflation over next 6 months
Source: CEIC, SEB
Despite holding policy steady, S$NEER will remain close to the upper bound as MAS has left the door open for further tightening. 
While MAS expects its Core CPI inflation to ease from mid-2027, it acknowledges that risks remain tilted to the upside. As it is, imported inflation remains elevated, keeping upward pressure to incoming inflation prints in the next six months (Chart 2). Even if energy production and shipments from the Middle East were to recover more quickly than MAS projected, policymakers remain wary of upward risks to food prices from El Niño which is expected to be strongest on record. Moreover, the annual gains in the S$NEER have failed to keep up with the MAS Core inflation despite the S$NEER hugging the upper policy band (Chart 3). This suggests the central bank’s work may not be done. 
Chart 3: Gains in S$NEER has not been enough to offset gains in MAS Core inflation
Source: Bloomberg, CEIC, SEB
MAS will likely resume tightening in 2027 should upside risks to inflation materialize
. Already, the central bank expects Core inflation to average at 1.5-2.5% in 2027 as compared to its latest 2026 forecast range of 1.5-2.0%. Imported price pressures remain above historical trends. Yet, the broader spread of inflation seems to be slowing. Our diffusion index of items with rising prices has retreated, which should cap MAS Core inflation over the coming months (Chart 4). This gives policymakers room for today’s pause. 
Chart 4: The diffusion of price pressures is starting to ease
Source: CEIC, SEB
With policy held steady today, the S$NEER has little room for a near-term rally, tilting upside risks to our end-2026 USD/SGD target of 1.26. 
While the policy band continues to rise at 1.25% pa, the S$NEER is already hugging the upper bound. This caps the room for USD/SGD to slide in the coming months, barring a sharp sell-off in the greenback. Yet, with balance of risks leaning toward further tightening rather than easing, any pullback in the Singdollar will be brief. The Singdollar should continue to outpace its regional peers. Year-to-date, it lags only the Korean won and the Chinese yuan.

articles.title: Fed comments lend hope to battered rate doves
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
Interest rates resumed their decline in the US yesterday following dovish comments from Fed's Williams, who expects rates to remain unchanged at the next meeting and still anticipates a hike in December, but currently sees no need for further increases next year. The dollar weakened broadly and Brent crude fell. Chinese data showed persistently low consumer inflation despite surprisingly elevated producer prices, pointing to weak domestic demand. Asian markets were mixed overnight, while US stocks closed slightly lower amid disappointing results from several major US banks and declines in semiconductor and chipmaker stocks. Futures point to a positive opening in Europe and the US. 
We start the day
 with Swedish inflation and household consumption data, but the main event is US CPI this afternoon. The IMF publishes its Fiscal Monitor, and several central bank officials are scheduled to speak throughout the day.
In this edition of Ögat
, we discuss the Fed's upcoming rate decision and assess Andy Burnham's first months as UK Prime Minister. We also examine France's strained public finances and share our views ahead of Spain's snap election. Finally, we look at how a weaker krona affects inflation and present the results of our latest SEK Views FX survey. Read more 
here 
(in Swedish).
This week's highlight: US inflation.
 High energy prices are expected to have lifted headline inflation to 3.7% y/y in September, while core inflation (excluding food and energy) likely edged up to 2.5%. Signs of rising goods prices have prompted us to raise our near-term inflation forecast. There are also indications that rents may start to pick up again, while wage growth continues to moderate. Markets have scaled back expectations for Fed tightening and no longer expect a hike this month. Both we and the market now see December as the most likely timing for the next hike, although a significant inflation surprise could change that outlook. Markets are still pricing about 80bps higher rates in the coming 12 months.
Nordic key stories
The krona strengthened broadly during the day, supported by lower yields and a weaker dollar.
 We believe speculative investors have been heavily positioned for SEK weakness but are now looking to scale back those positions. This means buying SEK, adding to its strength (for more on this: 
Sweden 360
).
Final Swedish September inflation, including details.
 The preliminary figures showed Swedish core inflation coming in below both our and the Riksbank's forecasts in September. Several factors suggest that the surprisingly large price increases over the summer were largely temporary. Underlying inflation is still expected to rise gradually over the coming year, but we see little signs of a marked acceleration in the near term. Read more 
here
.
Swedish household consumption.
 Retail sales and household spending have risen markedly over the summer, while consumer confidence has finally returned to more optimistic levels. We expect a slight dip in consumption in September, but the underlying momentum remains strong. Still, downwards risks to our relatively optimistic 2027 forecast are building. High energy prices, fading fiscal support and earlier Riksbank rate hikes have shifted the balance of risks to the downside.
Magdalena Andersson (Social Democrats) faces vote as Swedish PM tomorrow.
 Yesterday, Andersson stated she was unable to form a government. Nonetheless, parliament will vote at 12:00 local time on whether to appoint her prime minister of a single-party Social Democratic government, although she is almost certain to be voted down. The vote is intended to put pressure on the parties and speed up the process of forming a new government.

articles.title: Fed-kommentarer ger ränteduvorna luft under vingarna
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Gårdagen inleddes med räntenedgångar, som återupptogs i USA efter duvaktiga kommentarer från Fed-ledamoten Williams. Han signalerade oförändrad ränta vid nästa möte och tror fortsatt på en höjning i december, men ser i dagsläget inte behov av fler nästa år. Dollarn försvagades brett under dagen och Brentoljan sjönk. Kinesisk statistik på morgonen visade fortsatt låg konsumentinflation trots oväntat högt producentpristryck; ett uttryck för svag inhemsk efterfrågan. Asiatiska börser utvecklades blandat under natten. I USA stängde börserna svagt ned, tyngda av svaga rapporter från flera storbanker och nedgångar i halvledar- och chipbolag. Börsterminer pekar mot en positiv öppning i Europa och USA.
Vi inleder dagen 
med svensk inflation och hushållskonsumtion, men dagens höjdpunkt är amerikanska inflationssiffror senare i eftermiddag. IMF publicerar sin Fiscal Monitor och flera centralbanksledamöter håller tal under dagen.
I detta nummer av Ögat
 resonerar vi om Feds kommande räntebesked och analyserar Andy Burnhams första tid som brittisk premiärminister. Vi skriver också om Frankrikes ansträngda statsfinanser och ger vår syn på det stundande nyvalet i Spanien. Avslutningsvis beskriver vi hur en svagare krona påverkar inflationen och presenterar resultaten från vår enkät Kronsyn. Mer 
här
!
Veckans höjdpunkt: Amerikansk inflation.
 Höga energipriser väntas ha pressat upp totalinflationen till 3,7 procent i årstakt i september, medan kärninflationen (exkl. livsmedel och energi) troligen steg marginellt till 2,5 procent. Indikationer på stigande varupriser har fått oss att höja vår inflationsprognos i närtid. Det finns också tecken på att hyrorna kan börja stiga snabbare igen, medan löneinflationen fortsätter att avta. Marknaden har skruvat ned sina förväntningar på Fed och räknar inte längre med någon höjning redan denna månad. Både vi och marknaden ser i stället december som den mest sannolika tidpunkten, men en större inflationsöverraskning kan ändra bilden. 
Marknaden prisar fortsatt in runt 80 räntepunkter högre ränta kommande tolv månader.
Sverige
Kronan stärktes på bred front under dagen, hjälpt av lägre räntor och dollarsvaghet. 
Vår bild är att spekulativa aktörer har varit tydligt positionerade för en svagare krona, men nu vill minska dessa positioner. I praktiken innebär det kronköp och en starkare krona (lästips: 
Sweden 360
).
Slutliga tal och detaljer för septemberinflationen.
 Det preliminära utfallet visade att den svenska kärninflationen var lägre än både vi och Riksbanken hade räknat med i september. Flera faktorer tyder på att de oväntat stora prisuppgångarna under sommaren mestadels var tillfälliga. Den underliggande inflationen väntas ändå stiga gradvis under det kommande året, men vi ser få tecken på någon tydlig acceleration i närtid. Läs mer 
här
.
Svensk hushållskonsumtion.
 Detaljhandeln och hushållens konsumtion har stigit tydligt under sommaren, och konsumentförtroendet har äntligen nått mer optimistiska nivåer. En liten nedgång i konsumtionen är dock att vänta i september, men trenden är fortsatt stark. Samtidigt finns ett och annat orosmoln för vår relativt optimistiska prognos för 2027. Höga energipriser, avtagande finanspolitiskt stöd och tidiga räntehöjningar från Riksbanken gör att riskerna har skiftat mot nedsidan.
Magdalena Andersson (S) prövas som statsminister i morgon
. Under gårdagen meddelade Andersson att ”det saknas förutsättningar för att bilda en regering”. Hon kommer ändå att prövas som statsminister för en socialdemokratisk enpartiregering i morgon klockan 12, trots att hon nästan säkert röstas ned. Omröstningen genomförs för att sätta press på partierna och påskynda regeringsbildningen.

articles.title: Räntepaus väntas inför mellanårsvalet i USA
articles.heading: Ögat
articles.fulltext:
Senaste tidens händelser och uttalanden från amerikanska centralbanken Federal Reserve har fått marknaden att svänga om till att tro på oförändrad ränta vid räntebeskedet 28 oktober. Vi håller fast vid vår prognos om en avslutande höjning i december. Risken för prognosen ligger på uppsidan och möjligheten att Fed höjer ännu en gång nästa år. Feds ledamöter är splittrade om behovet av ytterligare åtstramning och marknaden tror på minst tre ytterligare höjningar, även om den bara prisar in en till i år. 
Försiktig budget i en orolig tid
Storbritanniens premiärminister Andy Burnhams första månader har varit lugnare än väntat. Löften om framtida reformer är dock många och omfattande, och budgeten den 28 oktober är sannolikt tänkt att lägga grunden för dessa. 
Fortsatt fransk marknadsoro och nyval i Spanien
Det råder fortsatt oro kring det statsfinansiella läget i Frankrike. Parlamentet ska enas om en budget för 2027 samtidigt som ytterkanterna laddar för presidentvalet nästa år. Spanien har nyval 29 november och rådande opinionsläge som indikerar ett regeringsskifte. 
Kronsyn: Svag krona – men optimismen lever
Den svenska kronan befinner sig i en betydligt tuffare omvärld. Högre räntor utomlands, geopolitisk oro och minskad riskaptit har försämrat förutsättningarna för en starkare krona. SEB:s senaste valutaenkät, Kronsyn, visar ändå att marknadens aktörer räknar med en kronförstärkning framöver. Mycket hänger på centralbankerna och utvecklingen i Mellanöstern. 
Hur påverkar en svagare krona inflationen?
En fråga vi ofta fått den senaste tiden handlar om i vilken grad Riksbanken kan avvika från ECB utan att orsaka en oönskad försvagning av kronan. Kopplingen till räntedifferensen går via frågan om vilken effekt en svagare krona får på svensk inflation. Vi bedömer att det krävs väldigt stora förändringar av växelkursen för att ge mer betydande genomslag i svensk inflation.

articles.title: NOK 3bn in NST480 and NST490
articles.heading: NGB Spotlight
articles.fulltext:
On Wednesday Oct 14th, Norges Bank will hold a multiple tap auction where a total of NOK 3bn will be issued, split between the NST480 (2.00%, 04/2028) and the NST490 (4.125%, 06/2036) bonds. NST480 currently trades with a yield of 4.8125%, implying a maturity-matched spread vs. Germany of 178bps and an ASW spread of -37.5bps. NST490 trades with a yield of 4.465%, with corresponding spread levels at 112bps and -10.5bps. The auction closes at 11.00 CET, and results will be available on Norges Bank’s website at 11.05 CET. 
On Wednesday, Norges Bank will auction a total of NOK 3bn split between NST480 (04/2028) and the NST490 (06/2036) bonds. Last week’s tap auction also included the 2028 bond, though combined with the new 20y bond. 
Market conditions are challenging given the global selloff and high volatility. Last week’s auction nonetheless went smoothly as both bonds cleared close to the offer side with decent bid-to-cover ratios. Another inclusion of NST491 would likely have been preferred, while primarily belly bonds remain offered via ASW. Outright yield level in NST480 and the cheapening of NST490 on a spread-basis vs. Germany suggest decent demand in the upcoming auction. 
In the previous 5 tap auctions including NST480, the bond received an average bid-to-cover of 4.49 with an allotment share of 59%. Corresponding numbers for the 9 auctions in NST490 are 3.60 and 56%.
The auction calendar implies new supply on a weekly basis in October. Overall, market sentiment remains the same as last week although a bit more neutral. Expectations for Norges Bank have eased a bit with the market discounting an 80% likelihood for another rate hike by March 2027. We reiterate our forecast that the policy rate peak has been reached.
Following this auction, Norges Bank has issued a total of NOK 97bn YTD, while the annual borrowing interval is set at NOK 100-110bn (107-110bn in the Q4 guidance). We expect Norges Bank to issue the maximum amount, implying another NOK 3bn in the following auction and NOK 2bn for the remaining 5 auctions.
The government’s budget proposal for 2027 showed an underlying borrowing requirement of NOK 93.6bn vs. 95.7bn in 2026. After years of under-borrowing, Norges Bank’s supply estimate has exceeded the underlying borrowing requirement over the past two years, with the aim of building up the cash reserves. We expect this to be the case also in 2027, implying a minimum of NOK 110bn in gross supply. The government’s borrowing mandate in long-term debt is increased by NOK 50bn to NOK 200bn, to provide greater flexibility and allowing for a potential increase in its own holdings. Risks to our supply estimate are thus skewed to the upside. Details will be provided in Norges Bank’s Strategy and borrowing programme due in December.

articles.title: Concerns about the growth of AI companies are lowering the stock market
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
After positive tones on the European stock exchanges yesterday, stock markets in the US declined, a development that gained further momentum during Asian trading this morning. As usual, technology companies are in the main focus. Ahead of the reporting season, worrying questions are now being asked whether the large AI investments can be backed up by growth. This is especially true now as investments are not only made on borrowed money, but also coincide with the recent sharp rise in interest rates. The decline in Japan is 2.5% while the South Korean KOSPI is down almost 7%. Stock market futures ahead of the opening in Europe and the US clearly point to negative numbers. Oil prices are falling slightly after three days of gains and are now trading around USD 105 per barrel, for more on the current situation see Bjarne's comment 
here
. 
Yesterday, German Chancellor Merz said that the government will reduce the tax on electricity to the EU's minimum level (from the current 2% to the equivalent of 0.05%). He pointed out that it is just as important to support households, as it is to make new long-term reforms.
Today's statistical calendar can be described as averagely interesting.
 The focus is on the details of German inflation statistics if they give a different picture than the overall figures published earlier. From the US, we are of course looking at the small business barometer, ADP employment and home sales. 
New IMF forecast
 under the heading "Resilience under pressure, urgent elections". The IMF has increased global growth by a tenth for this year. The message is that AI investments counteract the negative repercussions of high energy prices. Reduced inventory levels have also counteracted the lower supply of oil. The IMF also notes that the margins of the measures that have affected resilience are not unlimited, and points out that the risk picture is on the downside. The rapidly rising interest rates mean that the IMF urges that it is urgent to do something about the budget deficits. For more, much more, read 
here
.
A hint for the Fed governor?
 This year's economics laureates, Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford, have clarified the role of forward-looking expectations in how stabilization policy affects businesses and households, and are thus extremely close to the work we do. But the fact that they are receiving the award now, just as the new Fed Chair Warsh wants to make the Fed less transparent, is perhaps not a pure coincidence
